title: idp-profiles-security-hardening-and-rbac-integration
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Deliver IdP-specific compatibility profiles and hardened validation rules for Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and Ping so that SAML SSO + RBAC v2 integration is deterministic, auditable, and safe for tenant-admin operations. This ticket bundles: 1) standardized assertion validation and attribute normalization per IdP; 2) explicit mappings from IdP groups/claims to RBAC v2 roles; 3) audit events for admin-level SSO changes and group-sync actions; 4) admin console controls for IdP profile selection and certificate rotation policies. Motivation: Recent customer integration issues showed variations in NameID formats, group attribute encodings, and certificate rollover behaviors that caused RBAC mis-assignments or silent failures. We need a testable, documented compatibility matrix and safe defaults for production deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility profiles implemented for Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and Ping in SAML adapter with clear toggles in admin console
Assertion validator enforces signature algorithms and allows a configured list per-profile (RSA-SHA256 default) with graceful rejection and clear audit events
Attribute normalization rules for email/username/uid and group claims produce deterministic RBAC v2 role assignments in >= 95% of observed customer mappings
All admin-initiated SSO config changes (add/remove IdP, cert upload, profile switch) emit audit events with actor, timestamp, affected-tenant, and before/after snapshot
Group sync operations log delta events and expose failure reasons in the console and in the audit stream
Automated test matrix (end-to-end) covering at least one typical profile flow per IdP is added to CI and green
Docs updated: admin guide, troubleshooting playbook, and per-IdP appendix (Okta/Azure/Google/Ping) published and linked from console
implementation_steps: Draft IdP profiles spec: NameID formats, default signature algorithms, accepted certificate encodings, group attribute keys, session duration mapping
Implement profile selector in SAML adapter and add hooks into RBAC v2 mapping layer
Add attribute normalizer library with rulesets for each IdP; keep rules composable and testable
Instrument audit logger to capture SSO admin events and group-sync deltas (include payload size limits and PII redaction rules)
Add admin console UI changes: IdP profile dropdown, cert upload with preview, 'simulate assertion' tester for admins
Create CI e2e harness using test IdP fixtures (Okta dev org, Azure test tenant, Google Workspace test domain, Ping test deployment) and wire to nightly runs
Write documentation: admin quickstart, troubleshooting scenarios, known edge-cases per IdP and mitigation steps
Coordinate rollout with SRE and Security for monitoring and feature flag gating
test_plan: Unit tests: coverage for normalization rules and assertion validator error paths
Integration tests: simulated SAML response flows for each IdP profile with variations: NameID=email/persistent/transient, group-as-attribute vs group-as-assertion, SAML 2.0 bindings POST/Redirect
RBAC mapping tests: verify direct claim->role, nested-group resolution, and fallback to default role when mapping absent
Audit tests: verify audit entries are emitted on admin changes, group-sync deltas are recorded, and sensitive fields are redacted
Manual QA: run admin console simulator to exercise cert rotations and verify session continuity for existing active tokens
Canary: enable profile enforcement behind a feature flag for 10% of Hosted API tenants and monitor errors and support tickets for 72 hours
rollout_plan: Week 1: internal-only QA and SRE smoke tests in staging
Week 2: 10% canary on staging customer subset, monitor audit log volume and RBAC mismatches
Week 3: 50% expansion if metrics stable, provide opt-out for tenant-admins
Week 4: full rollout with updated docs and migration guide
Post-rollout: 30-day monitoring window and follow-up patch if group-sync edge cases surface

rbac_changes: Add deterministic claim-to-role mapping table and precedence rules: explicit group claim mapping > mapped email domain rules > default tenant role. RBAC v2 will accept a normalized 'subject_id' and 'groups' array; implement transactional role reconciliation with audit deltas.
audit_logging_changes: sso.idp_config_changed: emitted when tenant admin adds/removes or edits an IdP profile (include actor and diff)
sso.cert_rotated: emitted when a certificate is uploaded/rotated; record thumbprint and expiry (redact raw cert)
sso.assertion_validation_failure: emitted for rejected assertions with sanitized reason codes
sso.group_sync_delta: emitted after scheduled or on-demand group sync, includes counts (added/removed/errored)
admin.simulate_assertion: emitted when tenant-admin runs the simulate assertion tool
risks: Large tenants may emit high volume of group-sync events increasing audit storage and indexing costs
Aggressive normalization rules could mis-map custom IdP claims for niche customers; need opt-out and custom mapping support
Certificate rotation failures could cause outages if not handled with graceful fallback (cache TTLs and secondary certs)
RBAC reconciliation lag may temporarily remove access for in-flight sessions if not reconciled carefully
notes_for_oncall: If assertion_validation_failure spikes, toggle feature flag 'idp-profiles-v1' to off and engage security to examine recent IdP cert changes
Retention: do not store full SAML assertions in logs; store hashes and redacted fields only
